global_issues.title: Lighter Inflation Data Eases Yields, Lifts Stocks
global_issues.note: Confirmed: July PPI came in flat/below expectations (core PPI +0.2% vs +0.3% expected), 10-year yield eased ~1bp to 4.67%, S&P 500 closed at a record high (+0.65%), Nasdaq +0.8%, Dow +0.13% to 53,839.99 on Aug 13. Matches CNBC/NBC News reporting.

global_issues.title: Middle East Supply Risks Keep Oil Elevated
global_issues.note: Confirmed directionally: Iran/Hormuz talks remain deadlocked (Iran demanding sanctions relief and war reparations before reopening the strait), keeping a geopolitical premium in oil. Nuance the briefing omits: WTI actually fell ~2.4% on Aug 13 to ~$81.25 and Brent ~2% to ~$87 after the U.S. reported Hormuz crude exports near 9M bpd, i.e. a partial pullback from the prior 6-session, 12% run-up rather than straight-line 'elevated' pricing.

missing_major_news.impact: Directly relevant to NVDA (listed as 'watch') and broader AI-infrastructure names (MSFT, ANET, CRWD in leaders); a major bullish structural catalyst reported Aug 13 that the briefing's NVDA note and sector rotation commentary do not mention at all.

missing_major_news.impact: META is in the watchlist marked 'action=avoid' with a -0.35% close cited; the underlying driver (aggressive AI infra spend, well received by investors) is a notable positive catalyst not reflected in the briefing's framing of META.

grok_report.summary: The core inflation/yields/equities narrative and oil/Hormuz framing are both accurate and well-sourced, and the PLTR/MU standout gainers check out against real pricing. The main gap is omission of two market-moving AI-infrastructure stories from Aug 13 — Nvidia's $500B+ financing consortium and Meta's $130-145B capex guidance with new Muse models — both of which are directly relevant to watchlist names (NVDA, META) and would have strengthened the sector-rotation narrative the briefing already gestures at.
